title: Staged edge usage evacuation protocol for isolated deployments
creator: Amelia Chen
description:
Problem: Private/VPC and air-gapped customer deployments currently ship usage records in large monolithic bundles. These bundles are brittle to partial failures, cause long tail delays for downstream billing, and make rate-limit/quota reconciliation during delayed syncs error-prone. We need a deterministic, resumable 'staged evacuation' protocol that lets on-prem collectors stream compact chained segments out-of-band (USB/airdrop/s3 mirror) or via intermittent egress lanes while preserving token-level accounting, quota windows, and idempotency semantics.

Goal: Define and implement a protocol + local collector runtime changes that: 1) produce cryptographically anchored sequence segments (anchors + delta-encoding) that can be ingested idempotently by the billing ledger; 2) preserve per-token attribution to routes/models and quota windows so downstream enforcement and chargebacks remain correct; 3) provide compact backfill support for delayed syncs and partial replay; 4) integrate with existing quota windowing and rate-limit counters so we can compute effective throttle state for historical windows during reconciliation.

Success criteria: downstream billing ledger accepts staged segments with no conflicts for >99.9% of customer syncs; reconciliation runbook completes without manual fixes for common failure modes; total size of evacuation exports reduced by >=40% versus current full-bundle baseline.
acceptance_criteria: Collector emits signed sequence segments with monotonic sequence IDs per tenant
Ingest pipeline accepts segments out-of-order and applies them idempotently
Quota window attribution is preserved for each usage record in backfill mode
Partial segment failure can be resumed without double-charging or missing tokens
End-to-end tests cover intermittent egress (simulate USB + delayed upload) and ledger reconciliation
steps_taken: 11/05: Design spike — compared delta-encoding options (delta-by-session, delta-by-route, token-range diffs), chose token-range delta with sequence anchors for compactness
11/06: Proof-of-concept Python tool to produce chained segment files and SHA256 anchors
11/08: Collector runtime change prototype — local segment writer + manifest creator. Added tombstone markers for revoked sessions
11/09: Integration test harness that simulates partial transfer, interrupted copy, and duplicate segment ingestion
next_steps: Finish ingestion adapter in billing ledger to accept 'segment:anchor' format (backend PR open)
Add signed manifest verification and key rotation support for offline bundles
Wire-up runbook for customer support and create automatic recovery playbook entries
Performance test for typical private deployment (50k tokens/day) to validate size reduction and reingestion latency

notes_on_tradeoffs: We chose sequence anchors + token-range deltas over full session diffs to reduce size; tradeoff is added complexity when tokens cross quota boundaries — will handle via explicit boundary markers and an attribution pass during ingestion.
Using strong cryptographic anchors increases bundle size slightly but drastically lowers risk of tampering during physical transfer; acceptable for regulated customers.
Alternative: keep current monolithic bundles and add resumable transfer layer — rejected because it doesn't address ledger idempotency and cross-window attribution.
